verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev describes itself as an "Open source platform" in its llms.txt, and it has a public GitHub repository at triggerdotdev/trigger.dev with self-hostable code, so its source is readable. However, no evidence names the specific license or its terms, so the 'open license' part of the story is asserted rather than documented. missing for 10: explicit license identification (e.g., the LICENSE file or license name and terms), independent corroboration of the license's openness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Open source platform for durable, long-running tasks.
Execute your tasks with absolutely no timeouts, unlike AWS Lambda, Vercel, and other serverless platforms.
Self-hosting Trigger.dev means you run and manage the platform on your own infrastructure
